mcqs.q: What does Bentham's hedonic calculus measure?
options: The quantity of pleasure and pain produced, using factors such as intensity, duration and certainty
The cost of an action in money
Obedience to the Ten Commandments
The opinion of the majority in a vote

mcqs.q: For Fletcher's situation ethics, what is the only thing intrinsically good?
options: Agape love
Pleasure
Duty
Obedience to law

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of Aquinas's primary precepts?
options: The preservation of life
The maximisation of pleasure
The abolition of property
Obedience to the state in all things

mcqs.q: What does jus ad bellum concern?
options: Whether going to war is justified in the first place
How soldiers must behave during a war
How to rebuild a country after a war
Whether weapons may ever be manufactured

mcqs.q: Is utilitarianism just 'do whatever makes you happy'?
options: Utilitarianism commands obedience to religious authority.
Utilitarianism is a selfish philosophy of personal pleasure-seeking.
Natural law is the scientific study of gravity and motion.
No - it demands impartial maximisation of happiness for all affected, which can require serious personal sacrifice; the agent's own pleasure counts no more than anyone else's.

mcqs.q: Is situation ethics the same as having no rules at all?
options: Situation ethics requires obeying every rule without exception.
Fletcher taught that moral rules are worthless and anything goes.
Utilitarianism commands obedience to religious authority.
No - Fletcher rejected both legalism and antinomianism; rules are valuable 'illuminators' that should be set aside only when agape love requires it.

mcqs.q: Does natural law mean 'doing whatever comes naturally'?
options: Natural moral law tells us to follow our instincts.
Natural law is the scientific study of gravity and motion.
Utilitarianism commands obedience to religious authority.
No - Aquinas meant rational reflection on the purposes of human nature; some instinctive urges are contrary to reason and therefore against natural law.
